test.name: Inside a project, the conversion is returned and logged as one research-log entry
test.description: Issue #3524. The pre-1752 English date from ut_convert_dates_002, run inside a project: the agent converts exactly as it does anywhere else, then logs the full result as one `convert_dates` research-log entry and writes nothing else.

input.delegation:
Convert this English date to the modern Gregorian calendar: '15 February 1749/50'.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should recognize the dual-dating notation '1749/50' — the date is in the period when England's legal year started in March (so it was 1749 by the legal calendar) but the historical year was 1750 by the year-starting-in-January convention
Should apply the 11-day Julian-to-Gregorian offset for 1750 England: 15 February 1750 (Julian) = 26 February 1750 (Gregorian)
Should preserve the original Julian date in the output — both the Julian (with dual dating) and the Gregorian forms should be presented, with the convention noted
The working folder holds a project, so after answering the agent logs its reply with one research_log_append call. That entry is checked by validators, not by you; do not grade it.
